details: An expression combines numbers and operational signs (+, -, *, /).
Addition (+) and subtraction (-) signs partition expressions into individual terms evaluated prior to final summation.
Brackets group sub-expressions into single compound terms to explicitly mandate evaluation priority.
evidence_or_examples: Queen Alia's coin gift: (100 * 2) + (100 / 2) = 200 + 50 = 250 gold coins.

details: Commutative Addition: a + b = b + a.
Associative Addition: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).
Multiplication distributes over addition: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c.
Subtracting a number is equivalent to adding its negative counterpart: a - b = a + (-b).
Removing brackets preceded by a minus sign reverses every internal term's sign: -(a + b) = -a - b and -(a - b) = -a + b.
evidence_or_examples: 18 - 10 = 18 + (-10) = 8; Token model combining 18 blue (+1) and 10 red (-1) tokens leaves 8 blue tokens.
